moments.text: You spent Saturday painting for the first time in years.
You lost track of time and felt pure fun.
You showed a painting to a friend.
You noticed you felt proud and a bit shy.
You told Orca that making things just for fun used to feel selfish, and now it feels like breathing.
You signed up for an evening class and followed through.
You sat in the park after class and noticed you felt calm and happy.

moments.text: Zauważyłaś, że przed prezentacją w pracy cała się trzęsłaś i bałaś się oceny szefa.
Przed prezentacją w pracy i myśl o ocenie szefa nadal były dla ciebie trudne.
Zauważyłaś, że najtrudniejsze są pierwsze minuty.
Twoja terapeutka zaproponowała, żebyś na początku powiedziała jedno zdanie o tym, jak się czujesz.
Na spotkaniu zespołu powiedziałaś, że trochę się stresujesz, i od razu zrobiło się lżej.
Poprowadziłaś prezentację do końca.
Zgłosiłaś się do prowadzenia kolejnego spotkania, mimo że się bałaś.
Zauważyłaś, że byłaś też dumna.
Odpowiedziałaś szefowi wprost, że potrzebujesz więcej czasu na raport.
Wciąż trudno ci mówić to na głos przy wszystkich.

skills_full.name: Zauważanie pierwszych minut
skills_full.in_your_words: Widzisz, że najtrudniejsze są pierwsze minuty przed prezentacją. Zauważasz też, że ciało mocno reaguje, zanim jeszcze zaczniesz mówić.

skills_full.name: Mówić jedno zdanie na start
skills_full.in_your_words: Na początku mówisz jedno zdanie o tym, jak się czujesz, tak jak podpowiedziała twoja terapeutka. To pomaga ci wejść w spotkanie mimo strachu.

skills_full.name: Zgłaszać się mimo strachu
skills_full.in_your_words: Zgłaszasz się do prowadzenia spotkania, choć się boisz. Robisz to i zostajesz przy zadaniu.

moments.text: You keep picking up the phone to call your father, three months after he died.
You noticed you push sadness away by staying busy.
Your therapist suggested letting a wave come and pass without fixing it.
You looked at old photos and let yourself cry for a while.
You felt lighter afterwards.
You talked about the funeral and what you never said.
You wrote a letter to your father in the app.
You told your brother you miss your dad.
You talked with your brother for an hour, the first real talk in years.
You let the sadness come and went for a walk to his favourite bench.

skills_full.name: Letting grief come and pass
skills_full.in_your_words: You let the wave come without trying to fix it, and you stay with it until it passes. You also let yourself move through the feeling, like when you walked to his favourite bench.

skills_full.name: Saying what you miss
skills_full.in_your_words: You name that you miss your dad, and you bring up the funeral and what you never said. You also tell your brother what this loss feels like for you.

skills_full.name: Writing to him
skills_full.in_your_words: You use the app to write a letter to your father when there is so much left unsaid. It gives you a place to put the words you could not say out loud.

paths_full.name: Making room for my grief
paths_full.focus: about your father, the funeral, and missing him

hard_full.label: Picking up the phone to call your father
hard_full.context: When you reach for your phone, even though he died months ago.

moments.text: Working until midnight and feeling you had not done enough is still hard for you.
You noticed rest only felt allowed when you were ill.
You took Sunday morning off and read in bed.
You told yourself rest is part of the work.
You said something kind to yourself and went to bed early instead of pushing.
You noticed that another evening with nothing to earn felt easier.
You kept your Sunday morning rest anyway.

skills_full.name: Letting rest count
skills_full.in_your_words: You remind yourself that rest is part of the work, not something you only get when you are ill. You let yourself have an evening or morning off without needing to earn it first.

skills_full.name: Taking time off
skills_full.in_your_words: You make space for rest on purpose, like taking Sunday morning off and reading in bed. You try an evening with nothing to earn, and notice it can feel easier.

skills_full.name: Keeping Sunday morning rest
skills_full.in_your_words: You kept your Sunday morning rest anyway. You make time off count by letting it stay on the calendar and by choosing bed, reading, or a quiet morning instead of pushing through.

paths_full.name: Making room for rest
